a.text: Victoria is so close...
It's snowing again... they should be wearing their winter garb now.
She was like a little stove as a child, aflame with passion in her veins. This snow and wind won't faze her.
Baizao winters are never this cold. She said the first volume should be done when spring comes.
That's good...
At life's end, I find no worries left to bear.

steps.text: The man takes off his mandarin garb, folds it carefully. and places it down next to the books he used to carry, before bowing three times to the east.
He walks out of the camp.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Your flames are indeed hotter now.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Your Arts are greatly burdening your body, Infected.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Scared of the heat?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Heh, it's just my blood... Though I know I'm standing here only because so many others have shed their own blood.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Seems like you already know a lot.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Not much at all, but there's just one thing I need to know—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Those who had their names erased, those who died dubious deaths... they need an explanation, an answer.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: To be honest, I didn't think my life would have such a complicated backstory, or that I'd fight for something other than the Infected.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: But now I realize that injustice is the same for everyone. And I will spill my blood to end every injustice I encounter.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Burning a blaze with your blood... Infected, you resemble the righteous of old.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: But don't rush to conclusions about justice when a single leaf blocks your view of the entire forest.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: In any case, I have been ordered to bring you back, and you absolutely cannot be let free...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I know, I know... I've met your type before, plenty of times.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I guess I can't paint you all as bad guys. You've just been trained to shed no blood or tears... so you stop caring about anyone else's.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Whatever. I won't argue—you sure can try to stop me though.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: You are the enemy... but your courage deserves praise.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Careful now. I'll spare your life, but I can't guarantee you won't lose a limb or two.
Zongguan Bailei Zhengfa, cleave!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: It's you...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I know you have a lot of questions, but there's only one pressing matter at hand.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You wanted to see the True Lung, yes? I'm here to help.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Lin Qingyan? You should be behind bars!

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Yet I stand here before you now.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: You've already lost to me once. This time, neither of you will escape.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Don't worry, I have no plans to fight you alone.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: I know I asked to tag along...

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: But this opponent... will be hard to handle.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: An accomplice, even...

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: So you were the one who freed her from prison...

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: I had to employ some crude measures, but I tried my best to avoid harming any innocents.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Don't worry about settling the score. I have too many crimes I can't escape from, and this is just one more. When this matter is over, I will surrender myself to the law.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: But now, there is something to be done, and a meeting to be had.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: A Discipline and Supervision Censor colluding with a Judicial Review Office Deputy Minister in revolt... such a preposterous scene is a first for me.
If this is preposterous enough, then allow me to inconsequentially join the fray as well.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: I trust you've been well, Drillmaster?

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Taihe?! Were you not gravely wounded at Yumen—

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Yes... my injuries were quite serious. I'm unsure if my skills are even one-third as powerful as they used to be.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Which is why I hope there will be no cause for me to make any moves today.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Why would even you participate in this...?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: I have yet to grasp the full picture as to why Deputy Minister Lin has suddenly appeared here. But the two of you are my most respected colleagues, so I can only ask, as an old friend, that you two leave some space for negotiation.

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: How can you expect me to turn a blind eye when you lot insist on doing such a traitorous act?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: 'Loyalty over righteousness'... But whoever said you could only choose one from the two?

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Righteousness...

a.text: You're familiar with the case, and the two individuals involved in it stand here before you now.
Right or wrong, life or death. The choice is yours.
But Shifu... this matter came to be from complicated causes, how can what is good or evil be determined so easily—
The blade is in your hand. Make your choice!
Shifu...!
You hesitate still?!
Shifu, if 'righteousness' can only be upheld with the edge of my blade, then what sets it apart from 'violence'?
I don't understand...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Stop dallying and go inside!

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Don't even think about—

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: A signal to lower the Forbidden City's defenses...?

steps.name: Junior Drillmaster
steps.text: Could it be... His Imperial Majesty?

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: You can see the Forbidden City from here.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: It was still spring when I last set foot in this tower.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Much has happened within the last six months.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: The chill has come, and the wind atop the city walls is strong. Do take care of yourself, Grand Tutor.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: I imagine only a few from the court have seen Baizao from this angle.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Even from great heights, where the view stretches far, one's sight will sometimes be obscured by clouds.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: ...All the more reason that one should see and think before one acts.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Do you know why I asked you to become Advisor of Yumen?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: My thoughts were that you wanted me to broaden my horizons and see the big picture. An opportunity, but also a test.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: A test for what exactly?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: To see if I am worthy.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: So you know why I have summoned you here today?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Yes, Grand Tutor. You are disappointed in me.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: An excuse, or a genuine emotion?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I understand what I did during the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies was a terrible idea. But there was no other way.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Suspending the Feast will prevent the Grand Commandant from acting in drastic haste, and also allow the True Lung an opportunity.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Since your involvement in this slew of disputes, thrice have you been forced to make a choice, and each time you cast the riskiest die.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: You placed your friends and even yourself onto the chessboard... have you never once felt hesitation?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I dare not claim it never crossed my mind... but I have always considered the choice most beneficial for all.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: ...A capable plotter, but the same cannot be said for your decision-making.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: My plan was to select a young talent—ambitious but not greedy, resourceful but selfless—and give them many chances to hone themselves. If the chance arose, I would entrust them with significant responsibilities.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: I thought you were a suitable candidate... but it often does not end well when a chess player uses himself as a piece on the board.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: You remind me of a colleague... who is no longer with us.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I am humbled...

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: ...Liang Xun, given another chance, would you willingly leave Shangshu?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: When I started my studies, I was determined to apply my life's learning to the benefit of the people, regardless of whatever position I had gotten from mere chance...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: My original ambition remains, and I hold no regrets over the choices I made.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: The incident at the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies cannot go unpunished.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I will submit myself to the law.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: The Sky Mirror Pavilion's archive is lacking a transcriber, you will begin your duties there tomorrow morning.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: You have my gratitude, Grand Tutor.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: What is this...?

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: The time has come.
The clouds concentrate, completely obscuring the moonlight.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Have you met this one before...?

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Never.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Who exactly... is the opponent he seeks on this weiqi board...?

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: There are times when one seeks not an opponent to win against on the board, but a solution.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: A solution beneficial to both parties amid countless changes to the situation.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: There is something I wish to consult you on...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: What made you set up that exam in the first place?

steps.name: Passing Elder
steps.text: Shop's not closed yet, is it?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: You've come at the right time, I'll close right after I'm done with your order. It's late, so we don't have much left... but what would you like?

steps.name: Passing Elder
steps.text: Anything to fill up my stomach on the road will do.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: We happen to have half a steamer of meat buns here from the morning. You can have it for free.

steps.name: Passing Elder
steps.text: Won't you be making a loss like this?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I only know how to cook, not so good at business stuff.

steps.name: Passing Elder
steps.text: Why not earn a name and riches with skills like yours?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: What for? Both nobles and peasants eat the same three meals a day. I might as well make more buns than money or fame.

steps.name: Passing Elder
steps.text: If you don't mind another question, how much does a meal normally cost here?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Not much at all. The usual soup and two dishes just cost a few coins.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Anyone who works here in Baizao can eat their fill here.

steps.name: Passing Elder
steps.text: I see you have a kind heart and compassion for others.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Aw, stop that... I'm just a chef who serves about a hundred customers a day at most.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I can only count on you to feed and clothe everyone else in this realm.

steps.name: Passing Elder
steps.text: A free meal, and a lesson to boot... Lucky me.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Haha, I just hope you don't get mad at me. I just like aimlessly chatting with customers about everything under the sun.

steps.name: Passing Elder
steps.text: Your restaurant has been here a long time, if I'm not wrong. How are your finances?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Aiya... Now that's a headache. You see, this little store of mine can barely make even.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: It's all thanks to the abundant crops from Dahuang and the fast deliveries from the Chidao that I can keep my store running. Otherwise, I'd have to raise the prices.

steps.name: Passing Elder
steps.text: Are you sure you're not trying to give credit to your siblings?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Haha... but it doesn't stop here.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: My customers all live nearby. Some don't have enough coins, so they make up for it by sending me a few boxes of fresh fruit, or helping me repair the furniture...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Without their care, this restaurant wouldn't be running today.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: So, you see... It's hard to balance a book like this.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: But this is how you do business, right? Who says one side has to profit all the time? You give and you take. It's mutual prosperity that brings wealth and keeps the business thriving.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Your meat buns are ready and all packed, Grand Tutor. But why don't you try one now?

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Not bad at all.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: A word of advice. Don't take any more lessons from your businessman brother.

steps.name: Coachman
steps.text: Were you able to get a meal, sir?

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Yes. I heard the buns from this place are the best in Baizao. Try one yourself.

steps.name: Coachman
steps.text: Uh... hm... wow, it's delicious.

steps.name: Coachman
steps.text: Alright, I'm ready to get back on the road. Where to?

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Shangshu...

a.text: ...How do I get there again?
The seven streets and five lanes in the east of the city... I remember having to pass a dye workshop and a kiln first...
*sigh* My head hurts. It's been so many years; I wonder what changes—Oh? This calligraphy and painting store is still here? Surely their store sign can nearly be considered a historical relic...
I could come back again for a stroll. Who knows, I might just find it—on second thought, I probably couldn't if I tried.
Phew, almost there...
This ancient temple hasn't changed at all. No one's been here in years, but it hasn't been torn down either... Just who is feeling nostalgic for it?
The lock's already opened?
Oh, you're back.
